title: A CI step that compares command outputs must fail when a command fails
rule: When a workflow step captures a command's output to compare it (hashes, versions, counts), give the step `shell: bash` and `set -euo pipefail`, do not pipe the command through a filter (`| tail`, `| head`) inside `$(...)`, and validate the shape of each captured value (e.g. `^[0-9a-f]{64}`) before comparing. A plain `run:` is `bash -e` without pipefail, so a failed command behind a pipe leaves the step green and two equal error outputs compare as a match. Put the compare in a script function with unit tests for an empty line, a non-value line and a mismatch, and keep a test that checks the step's shell and the absence of the pipe.
rationale: E18.4 (#132): the fm-cli reproducibility job read `$(node build.mjs cli | tail -n 1)`; when both builds failed, both values were the echoed `$ cargo build …` line, `${a%% *}` matched `${b%% *}`, and the job went green with hash `$`.
